title: Harness reads accept an arbitrary statePath from the query
body:
## Summary
GET /api/harness and both screenshot routes read run files from any directory named by ?statePath=.

## Description
src/app/api/harness/route.ts:231, src/app/api/harness/screenshot/route.ts:19 and src/app/api/harness/screenshots/route.ts:28 take statePath from the query. The screenshot header calls the route "strictly path-jailed", but only slug and iter are jailed; the root itself is the caller's. Fixed = a statePath resolves to one recorded in harness_runs or the live config, otherwise 400.

## Flow
- GET /api/harness/screenshots?statePath=<any dir>
- the route lists <dir>/screenshots and parses each result.json
- fix: resolve statePath against the known run roots before any read

## Expected impact
Harness reads stop reaching directories no run owns. A caller inspecting a statePath from a run whose row was deleted would be refused.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - reads confined to known run roots
Before: 3 of 3 statePath reads take an unconfined path (read in code)
After: not taken - needs the run-root lookup and a decision on deleted rows
Method: simulation - code path read and walked this round; no instrument was built, so nothing was measured on both sides
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: policy-tighten
impact: Harness reads stop reaching directories no run owns. A caller inspecting a statePath from a run whose row was deleted would be refused.
instrument: route test: statePath outside every recorded run root -> 400 and no fs read; a recorded root -> 200

title: Screenshot enumeration reads a corrupt result.json as no modules
body:
## Summary
GET /api/harness/screenshots swallows a parse failure and reports the iteration with an empty module list.

## Description
src/app/api/harness/screenshots/route.ts:63 catches the parse error and continues. The sibling progressResponse in src/app/api/harness/route.ts states the contract: a corrupt file is not a legitimate empty. Fixed = the iteration row carries a corrupt marker the gallery shows.

## Flow
- a visual gate writes a truncated result.json
- GET /api/harness/screenshots answers modules: []
- the gallery shows an iteration that captured nothing
- fix: add corrupt: true to the row and render it in HarnessVisualGallery

## Expected impact
An operator can tell a damaged gate record from an empty one. An additive field, so existing readers are unaffected.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - corrupt evidence is reported as corrupt
Before: 1 of 2 harness sidecar reads honours the corrupt state
After: not taken - the gallery is outside this context
Method: simulation - code path read and walked this round; no instrument was built, so nothing was measured on both sides
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence: src/app/api/harness/screenshots/route.ts:63  } catch { /* fall through with empty modules */ }
impact: An operator can tell a damaged gate record from an empty one. An additive field, so existing readers are unaffected.
instrument: route test with an unparseable result.json asserting corrupt: true, plus a gallery render test

title: Regression dismiss and resolve report success for unknown ids
body:
## Summary
POST /api/regression-tracker answers dismissed or resolved true when no row matched.

## Description
dismissAlert and markResolved (src/lib/regression-tracker.ts:668, :674) discard the UPDATE change count, so src/app/api/regression-tracker/route.ts:82 and :89 cannot tell a hit from a miss. Fixed = both return changes > 0 and the route answers 404 on a miss.

## Flow
- POST { action: "dismiss", alertId: "nope" }
- UPDATE touches 0 rows
- route answers { dismissed: true }
- fix: return the change count and 404 on zero

## Expected impact
A stale client learns its target is gone. A client that relied on a miss being 200 would see a 404.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a success reply means the row changed
Before: 2 of 2 actions claim success on a 0-row UPDATE (read in code)
After: not taken - the lib is outside this context
Method: simulation - code path read and walked this round; no instrument was built, so nothing was measured on both sides
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
src/lib/regression-tracker.ts:671  db.prepare('UPDATE regression_alerts SET dismissed = 1 WHERE id = ?').run(alertId);
src/app/api/regression-tracker/route.ts:82  return apiSuccess({ dismissed: true });
impact: A stale client learns its target is gone. A client that relied on a miss being 200 would see a 404.
instrument: route test against an in-memory DB: unknown id -> 404, known id -> 200 and the row changed

title: Profiling sessions accumulate without a bound
body:
## Summary
The performance-profiling route keeps every imported or generated session in a process Map with no eviction.

## Description
src/app/api/performance-profiling/route.ts:13 holds full ProfilingSession objects; the only removal is the explicit delete-session action. Fixed = a retention cap, or persisted sessions, with the oldest evicted and reported.

## Flow
- repeated import-csv or generate-sample calls
- sessions.set at :51 and :72 with no eviction
- heap grows until restart
- fix: cap the Map and evict oldest with its triage

## Expected impact
A long-lived dev server stops growing with each capture. Evicting silently would lose a capture an operator still wants to compare, so the cap needs a visible signal.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - bounded session memory
Before: 0 eviction sites besides explicit delete (read in code); heap not measured
After: not taken - needs a chosen cap and a heap figure
Method: simulation - code path read and walked this round; no instrument was built, so nothing was measured on both sides
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
impact: A long-lived dev server stops growing with each capture. Evicting silently would lose a capture an operator still wants to compare, so the cap needs a visible signal.
instrument: test importing cap+1 sessions asserting the oldest is gone and list-sessions reports the cap

title: A start over a paused run orphans that run
body:
## Summary
POST start refuses only while status is running, so it replaces a paused in-memory orchestrator.

## Description
src/app/api/harness/route.ts:346 guards on running alone. A start with a different statePath overwrites globalForHarness.harnessOrchestrator while the paused run's row stays open with nothing able to resume it in memory. Fixed = 409 naming the paused run unless the caller passes an explicit override, or the paused run is settled first.

## Flow
- run A is paused
- POST start with statePath B
- the orchestrator global is replaced
- run A can only return through disk rehydrate, which needs its statePath

## Expected impact
A paused run cannot be displaced by accident. The controls panel guard (startGuard) would need the same rule, and a deliberate replace needs a path.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a paused run stays reachable
Before: 1 of 2 live statuses (running, paused) refuse a start
After: not taken - the override semantics are a product call shared with the panel
Method: simulation - code path read and walked this round; no instrument was built, so nothing was measured on both sides
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
src/app/api/harness/route.ts:346  if (globalForHarness.harnessStatus === 'running') {
src/components/harness/HarnessRunControls/controlGuards.ts:38  startGuard blocks only running
impact: A paused run cannot be displaced by accident. The controls panel guard (startGuard) would need the same rule, and a deliberate replace needs a path.
instrument: route test: paused status + start -> 409 and the orchestrator global unchanged

title: Deleting a harness run does not check that it is live
body:
## Summary
DELETE /api/harness/runs/:id drops the row of a run still executing.

## Description
src/app/api/harness/runs/[id]/route.ts:24 calls deleteRun unconditionally, and deleteRun (src/lib/harness-runs-db.ts:506) has no status filter. The orchestrator keeps writing to a row that no longer exists. Fixed = 409 while the id is the live run.

## Flow
- a run is executing
- DELETE its row
- later progress updates match no row and history loses the run
- fix: compare with the live orchestrator runId before deleting

## Expected impact
Run history cannot lose an in-flight run. No in-tree UI calls this DELETE today, so the exposure is API and MCP callers.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - live runs keep their record
Before: 0 liveness checks on the delete path (read in code)
After: not taken - the live run id is held by the harness route module
Method: simulation - code path read and walked this round; no instrument was built, so nothing was measured on both sides
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
src/app/api/harness/runs/[id]/route.ts:24  const ok = deleteRun(id);
src/lib/harness-runs-db.ts:508  DELETE FROM harness_runs WHERE run_id = ?
impact: Run history cannot lose an in-flight run. No in-tree UI calls this DELETE today, so the exposure is API and MCP callers.
instrument: route test: DELETE of the live run id -> 409 and the row kept

title: Paid vision verify routes are not operator-guarded
body:
## Summary
POST /api/verify/visual and /api/verify/animation read a caller-named local file and spend a metered vision call with no requireOperator.

## Description
src/app/api/verify/visual/route.ts:101 and src/app/api/verify/animation/route.ts:23 have no guard, and the visual route also records a verdict and emits eval.visual. A text/plain cross-site POST needs no preflight. Not built because the brief scopes the guard to process-spawning writes, and these are called by dispatched CLI sessions and scripts/anim-critique.mjs, none of which send a token. Fixed = both guarded, with those callers sending the token when one is configured.

## Flow
- a cross-site POST names a local PNG
- the route reads it and calls the vision router
- fix: requireOperator first, and pass the token from the CLI prompt and the script

## Expected impact
A foreign page can no longer spend vision budget or file a verdict. Under POF_OPERATOR_TOKEN, a caller that was not updated gets a 401.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - metered calls need an operator
Before: 0 of 2 verify routes guarded
After: not taken - callers must be updated together with the guard
Method: simulation - code path read and walked this round; no instrument was built, so nothing was measured on both sides
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: policy-tighten
impact: A foreign page can no longer spend vision budget or file a verdict. Under POF_OPERATOR_TOKEN, a caller that was not updated gets a 401.
instrument: route tests: cross-site 403, token required when set, header-less admitted; a script test that the token is forwarded
